subsystems.name: Reflective surface
subsystems.role: a vast, thin mirror that intercepts part of the star's light and throws it back in one direction.
parts: reflective film (a few micrometres thick in designs)

subsystems.name: Support structure
subsystems.role: holds the huge sheet in shape and connects it into a single piece large enough to enclose part of the star.

subsystems.name: Station-keeping and attitude control
subsystems.role: the mirror is balanced between the star's gravity and the push of its own light, an equilibrium that is unstable and must be actively held.

subsystems.name: Metrology and command
subsystems.role: knows where the mirror is and how it is tilted, from across a solar system.

subsystems.name: Material supply chain
subsystems.role: there is no ore to buy; the mirror has to be made from other bodies in the same system.
parts: refining and film production in microgravity

buildSteps.title: Choose a host star
buildSteps.detail: Pick a single, stable, long-lived star and map everything orbiting it — the raw material will come from those bodies.

buildSteps.title: Mine and refine in space
buildSteps.detail: Disassemble small moons or asteroids, extract metals and silicates, and refine them without ever touching a planet's gravity well.

buildSteps.title: Make the mirror film
buildSteps.detail: Produce extremely thin reflective sheet at industrial scale in orbit, since launching it from a surface would be impossible in the quantity needed.

buildSteps.title: Assemble panels into a shell
buildSteps.detail: Join panels into a partial hemisphere, shaped so the star sits at the focus and reflected light leaves roughly parallel.

buildSteps.title: Place it at the balance distance
buildSteps.detail: Position the mirror so that the outward push of starlight on it exactly cancels the star's pull inward, and keep it there.

buildSteps.title: Stabilise and steer
buildSteps.detail: Actively correct the unstable equilibrium; tilt or vary the reflectivity to shift the direction of net thrust.

buildSteps.title: Coast for millions of years
buildSteps.detail: The resulting acceleration is minuscule, so the whole planetary system drifts, slowly, on a chosen course.

buildSteps.title: Consider alternatives
buildSteps.detail: Concept designs that focus starlight into a jet of accelerated plasma would give much more thrust, at the cost of consuming the star's mass.

prerequisites.why: solar sails have flown, but at tens of metres — not the continent-scale areas required here.
the mirror's mass is far beyond anything that could be lifted from Earth; it must be built in space from local material.
signals take minutes to hours to arrive, so the structure has to correct its own instability itself.
operation is measured in millions of years, far beyond any engineered lifetime today.

pathway.milestone: solar sails and large unfurlable reflectors in space
pathway.unlocks: basic experience with light pressure as a controllable force.

pathway.milestone: in-space mining and orbital manufacturing at scale
pathway.unlocks: the ability to build megastructures without launching mass from Earth.

pathway.milestone: Dyson-swarm style collectors around a star
pathway.unlocks: the construction techniques and material supply that a thruster needs.

pathway.milestone: a partial stellar mirror held at light-pressure equilibrium
pathway.unlocks: moving an entire planetary system — slowly, and in one direction — over geological timescales.
